# Sanskrit cardinals, in RBNF (UTS #35 Part 3 §6), for `intl.inWords`.
#
# A DRAFT the SDK wrote, not CLDR's (CLDR 48 has no sa.xml): every word
# here waits for the consumer's Sanskrit reviewer (QUESTIONS.md Q42) and
# every answer spelt from it says `isDraft`. Hand-kept: `cargo xtask gen
# intl` reads this file, drops the lines starting `#`, parses the rest with
# the engine's own parser and writes `crates/intl/src/words/drafted.rs`.
# Change the words here, never in the generated file.
# docs/03-design/amounts-in-words.md §5 gives the reasoning; C1310 to
# C1319 the choices a reviewer is asked to confirm.
#
# Sources:
#   K  M. R. Kale, A Higher Sanskrit Grammar (1894; 7th ed. 1931),
#      §159 (the cardinals 1 to 99, 100, 200, 300, 1000, and the scale
#      words with their genders), §160 (Panini VI.3.47-49: dvi, tri and
#      astan become dva, trayas and asta before -vimsati and -trimsat, and
#      optionally from -catvarimsat on, never before asiti), §161 (the
#      numbers between the hundreds by adhika, "generally", and the worked
#      values 101, 112, 150, 1892 and 177639).
#   W  W. D. Whitney, A Sanskrit Grammar (1879; 2nd ed. 1889), §475 (the
#      decimal names; d: "in modern time the only numbers in practical use
#      above thousand are laksa and koti", an Indian sum counted in
#      crores, lakhs and thousands), §476 (11 to 99 and their sandhi), §477
#      (una and adhika), §481 (a multiplier compounded with sata or sahasra,
#      "in later usage more generally"), §§482-485 (inflection: sata and
#      sahasra neuter, the tens feminine).
#   L  Bhaskara's Lilavati v. 10-11 (K §159's footnote): eka, dasa, sata,
#      sahasra, ayuta, laksa, prayuta, koti, ... each ten times the last.
#
# How a number reads (K §161): the remainder below the largest scale,
# itself so read, compounded with adhika ("exceeded by"), then the scale
# word with its multiplier compounded (W §481: dvisatam, not dve sate),
# the whole one compound in the neuter (or, for koti, feminine)
# nominative singular:  1892 = dvanavaty-adhika-asta-sata-adhika-sahasram.
# The scales are those of the Indian grouping alone, sata, sahasra, laksa,
# koti (W §475 d), and kotis are counted with a full number (W §475 d's
# "1-23 crores"), so every i64 is spelt.
#
# A `+` marks where one substitution's text meets the next's inside the
# compound. The speller removes it, and where the text before it ends in
# a consonant's inherent a and the text after it starts with a vowel it
# writes the vowel sandhi (a + a = aa, a + e = ai: adhika+asta =
# adhikaasta, K §161's dvanavatyadhikaastasatadhikasahasram). Every other
# sandhi is spelt out in the rules themselves.

%spellout-cardinal:
-x: ऋणम् >>;
0: शून्यम्;
1: एकम्;
2: द्वे;
3: त्रीणि;
4: चत्वारि;
5: =%%stem=;
20: [>%%p20>]विंशतिः;
30: [>%%p30>]त्रिंशत्;
40: [>%%p40>]चत्वारिंशत्;
50: [>%%p50>]पञ्चाशत्;
60: [>%%p50>]षष्टिः;
70: [>%%p50>]सप्ततिः;
80: अशीतिः;
81: >%%p80>शीतिः;
90: नवतिः;
91: >%%p90>वतिः;
100: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<शतम्;
1000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<सहस्रम्;
100000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-l<लक्षम्;
10000000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-k<कोटिः;

# A number compounded with adhika: the remainder of the rule above.
%%adhika:
1: एकाधिक;
2: द्व्यधिक;
3: त्र्यधिक;
4: चतुरधिक;
5: पञ्चाधिक;
6: षडधिक;
7: सप्ताधिक;
8: अष्टाधिक;
9: नवाधिक;
10: दशाधिक;
11: एकादशाधिक;
12: द्वादशाधिक;
13: त्रयोदशाधिक;
14: चतुर्दशाधिक;
15: पञ्चदशाधिक;
16: षोडशाधिक;
17: सप्तदशाधिक;
18: अष्टादशाधिक;
19: नवदशाधिक;
20: [>%%p20>]विंशत्यधिक;
30: [>%%p30>]त्रिंशदधिक;
40: [>%%p40>]चत्वारिंशदधिक;
50: [>%%p50>]पञ्चाशदधिक;
60: [>%%p50>]षष्ट्यधिक;
70: [>%%p50>]सप्तत्यधिक;
80: अशीत्यधिक;
81: >%%p80>शीत्यधिक;
90: नवत्यधिक;
91: >%%p90>वत्यधिक;
100: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<शताधिक;
1000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<सहस्राधिक;
100000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-l<लक्षाधिक;
10000000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-k<कोट्यधिक;

# A multiplier's stem before sata and sahasra (and the nominative of 5 to
# 19, which is the bare stem, K §159): 1 is left out (satam, sahasram).
%%stem:
1: ;
2: द्वि;
3: त्रि;
4: चतुः;
5: पञ्च;
6: षट्;
7: सप्त;
8: अष्ट;
9: नव;
10: दश;
11: एकादश;
12: द्वादश;
13: त्रयोदश;
14: चतुर्दश;
15: पञ्चदश;
16: षोडश;
17: सप्तदश;
18: अष्टादश;
19: नवदश;
20: [>%%p20>]विंशति;
30: [>%%p30>]त्रिंशत्;
40: [>%%p40>]चत्वारिंशत्;
50: [>%%p50>]पञ्चाशत्;
60: [>%%p50>]षष्टि;
70: [>%%p50>]सप्तति;
80: अशीति;
81: >%%p80>शीति;
90: नवति;
91: >%%p90>वति;

# Before laksa, a voiced l: catur, sad, and -sat assimilated to -sal.
%%before-l:
1: =%%stem=;
4: चतुर्;
5: =%%stem=;
6: षड्;
7: =%%stem=;
30: [>%%p30>]त्रिंशल्;
40: [>%%p40>]चत्वारिंशल्;
50: [>%%p50>]पञ्चाशल्;
60: =%%stem=;

# Before koti: catus, and from 100 a whole number's compound stem.
%%before-k:
1: =%%stem=;
4: चतुष्;
5: =%%stem=;
100: =%%compound=;

# A number of 100 or more as the first member of a compound.
%%compound:
100: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<शत;
1000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%stem<सहस्र;
100000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-l<लक्ष;
10000000: [>%%adhika>+]<%%before-k<कोटि;

# The unit before each ten (K §159, W §476): dva and trayas before
# -vimsati and -trimsat, and from 40 by the first of K's two forms.
%%p20:

3: त्रयो;

6: षड्;

9: नव;
%%p30:

6: षट्;
7: =%%p20=;

3: त्रयश्;

6: षट्;

%%p50:

3: त्रयः;

5: =%%p20=;
6: षट्;
7: =%%p20=;
# Before asiti, with its a: unchanged dvi and tri (K §160).
